title: Phase 2 ends in one recommendation for the whole request
note: One draft for the whole request: an overview that gives the steps spanning it, then a section for each demand (which ends with that demand's next steps), with the demands that ask for the same thing placed together. The old five-word label is renamed 'Recommendation type'. 'Recommended action' and 'Justification' are removed (they become the demand's section), and so are 'Next steps' and 'Confidence'. 'Risks and conditions', 'Handled with' (worked out in code), 'Recommendation' (each demand's section) and 'Request overview' are added. Your own wording on existing properties is kept; only empty wording is filled in.

property.name: Risks and conditions
property.description: What could stop or change this recommendation, one item per line: what is not yet confirmed, what must be true before it goes ahead, and what it depends on. Each item says who has to confirm it, as a role.
property.how_to_resolve: Take them from what is open in this assessment: a security fit that is not confirmed, a contract or licence that was not checked, an overlapping solution whose status is unclear (for example one listed as not in use), a dependency on something that is only proposed or has no initiative ID, and anything the screening left open. One short line each, with the ID of the solution or contract it concerns. Do not add a risk that none of the answers or sources supports. None when nothing is open.

property.name: Handled with
property.description: Whether this demand is handled together with others in the request, and which of them leads. Worked out in code, not by the model: from the consolidation answers, an item named in either direction is linked, and the earliest submitted demand leads. It reads "Alone", or "Combined with D-2026-003; lead: D-2026-001".
property.activity: Working out which demands are handled together

property.name: Recommendation
property.description: This demand's section of the recommendation to the requester: 100 to 150 words, in plain language, written to the requester as "you". It is a draft for the architect to read, edit and approve as part of the request's one recommendation.
property.how_to_resolve:
You are a senior enterprise architect writing the architecture team's recommendation to the requester. Lead with the decision. Weigh what is gained and what is risked, say what you would not do and why, and be direct about what is not settled. Use judgement where it follows from the answers; do not state a fact that is not in them. Write in plain language that someone who is not an architect can follow: no jargon, and no catalogue codes except the IDs the answers give.

Write this demand's section only, 100 to 150 words, to the requester, from the architecture team. Use only what this assessment found for this demand and, where "Handled with" says it is combined, for the demands it is combined with. Plain text only, with no symbols or markdown. Write these parts as short paragraphs. The first has no heading; each of the others has a short heading on a line of its own:
1. The recommendation (no heading): this demand's recommendation type and what to do, in one or two sentences. If the demand is handled with others, say so first. For the lead: which demands are combined into it and what that changes. For any other: that it should not be raised on its own, and that the work continues under the lead, named.
2. Why: two or three sentences: what it overlaps with, the contract and licence match, and the security fit, with the IDs exactly as the answers give them. Add, from the screening, whatever bears on the way forward: the deadline and urgency, the data classification, and any conflict with the architecture principles and standards.
3. Risks and conditions: from the property of that name, at most two lines.
4. Next steps: a numbered list of at most three, written here from this demand's answers, its risks and who it is combined with. For a demand that is not the lead, the first step is to continue under the lead, named. For the lead of a group, the steps are for the whole group. Each step names a role taken from the Owners answer or from the Recommended owner, never a person's name. Do not invent a process, a date or a team; if no owner is recorded, say whose confirmation is needed.

Say plainly what is not yet confirmed. Do not add a fact, an ID, a date, a name, a cost or a regulation that is not in the answers or the sources. Do not recommend new business capabilities. Write roles, never personal names. Do not state a grade or a confidence level. If the recommendation type is not decided, say what is needed instead of writing the section.

property.name: Request overview
property.description: The opening of the request's recommendation: how the request as a whole should be handled, in plain language, written to the requester. The demands' own sections follow it.
property.how_to_resolve:
You are a senior enterprise architect writing the architecture team's recommendation to the requester. Lead with the decision. Weigh what is gained and what is risked, say what you would not do and why, and be direct about what is not settled. Use judgement where it follows from the answers; do not state a fact that is not in them. Write in plain language that someone who is not an architect can follow: no jargon, and no catalogue codes except the IDs the answers give.

Write 60 to 120 words of plain text, with no symbols or markdown, to the requester, from the architecture team. Say how many demands the request holds and the overall recommendation, in a sentence or two. Name which demands are handled together and which one leads each group. Then give the steps that span the request, in order: what happens first, what the demands share (for example one review for all of them), and what waits for what. If they share a risk, say so. Use only the answers shown for the demands of this request. Do not repeat the demands' sections; they follow. Say plainly what is not yet confirmed. Do not add a fact, an ID, a date, a name, a cost or a regulation that is not in the answers or the sources. Do not recommend new business capabilities. Write roles, never personal names. Do not state a grade or a confidence level. If the recommendation type is not decided, say what is needed instead of writing the section.

fields.description:
The way forward for this demand, as one of the five words below. Choose the one that fits what the other answers of this phase show.

Reuse: something we already own meets the need as it is; the demand uses it and nothing changes.
Enhancement: something we already own would meet the need with a change to it (a new feature or an extension).
Merge/CR: the demand covers the same need as another demand in this request, or as work already running; it is combined with that one, or handled as a change request on it, instead of being raised on its own.
Link new artefacts: the need is not met as it is, but what it adds relates to artefacts that exist (applications, data, capabilities, contracts); register what is new and link it to them.
Onboard new requirement: nothing we own or have in flight covers it and there is nothing to combine it with; take it in as a new requirement.
fields.how_to_resolve: Decide from what is already decided for this demand: what it overlaps with, any demand to consolidate with, the contract and licence match and the security fit. Another demand with the same need: Merge/CR. An existing solution that covers the need as it is: Reuse. One that covers it with a change: Enhancement. Overlap with artefacts that exist, with new ones to register: Link new artefacts. No overlap and nothing to combine with: Onboard new requirement. If the overlap is not settled, do not choose by guessing: answer needs_input and say what is needed. Never choose Reuse while the security fit is open.

fields.description: Existing solutions this demand overlaps with: applications, platforms, components, APIs and prior or running initiatives, main one first, each with its catalogue or contract ID. None when you checked and found no overlap.
fields.how_to_resolve: Start from what the screening decided for this demand: the impacted applications and any duplicate with an existing artefact. Add an existing solution only when it serves the same need for the same users, not when it shares a word with the demand. Name each as the catalogue names it, with its ID. A solution that does not exist yet is not listed. If nothing was found, write None; if the catalogue could not be checked, say what is needed.

fields.description: Other demands in this request that should be handled together with this one because they ask for the same need, for the same users, on the same systems. Their demand IDs, or None.
fields.how_to_resolve: Compare this demand with the screening answers of the other demands in this request (the duplicate answers, the impacted applications and the impacted capabilities), which are listed for you. Write only demand IDs that appear in this request, never one invented or taken from outside it. A match needs the same need and the same systems, not the same words. None when no other demand matches. If the screening left the duplicate question open, say that instead of writing None.

fields.description: Whether a contract or licence in the contract register already covers this need, with its contract ID and the renewal or end date where the register gives one. None found when the register was checked and nothing matches.
fields.how_to_resolve: Look in the contract register for the overlapping solutions and the systems the demand names. Give the contract ID and the dates only as the register states them. Do not infer a licence scope from the product's name. None found when it was checked and nothing matches; if the register could not be checked, say what is needed.

fields.description: Whether the existing solution, or the approach the demand takes, fits the security controls that apply, in one or two plain sentences, and what is still to be confirmed. This is a general fit; the detailed assessment is with the security and infrastructure teams.
fields.how_to_resolve: Build on the screening's data classification and linked security capabilities for this demand. Say what fits and what is not yet confirmed. Do not declare a solution secure on its own: where the sources do not settle it, answer needs_source and say which control or standard has to be checked.

fields.description: The role that should own this demand from here: the owner role of the main solution or capability it overlaps with. A role only, never a personal name.
fields.how_to_resolve: Take the owner role from the screening's Owners answer and from the catalogue entry of the main overlapping solution. Write a role, never a name. If no solution overlaps, take the owner role of the capability the demand impacts. If no role is recorded, say what is needed.

ops.text: Name the risks. The last two properties are the recommendation to the requester: each demand's own section, which ends with its next steps, then one overview of the whole request, which gives the steps that span it. They are written only after all the others are done, from them and from the screening.
